page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is generally limited, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. However, multi-core scaling is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores reaching average tiers. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average range, measuring 60.46 GB/sec for large block reads and 45.41 GB/sec for writes. Computational tasks such as software compilation and image processing achieve average performance, while single-threaded compression and text processing tasks perform poorly.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, the ecs.n4.2xlarge offers a budget-friendly entry point for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves average throughput, and lightweight Redis deployments. It is less suitable for heavy database operations, large language model inference, or single-threaded processing tasks due to its lower single-core performance and weak database benchmark results.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtual server featuring 8 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz. Operating on a shared CPU allocation model under KVM virtualization, it lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between weak single-core capabilities and average multi-core execution, with solid results in software compilation, image processing, and static web serving. Conversely, database operations and single-threaded compression tasks show weaker performance. This instance represents a budget-conscious option for multi-threaded workloads, lightweight Redis caching, and basic web serving, but is not recommended for intensive database hosting or single-threaded computational tasks.
